idiom_name: switch over a type tag with a throwing default (runtime only)
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no sealed types and no compile-time coverage check, so the pattern's promise - the compiler refuses an incomplete match - cannot be delivered. The most a plain module can do is a discriminated object ({ kind: 'circle', ... }) switched on its tag with a default arm that throws, which converts a missed case into an immediate failure but only at run time and only on executed paths. There is no Visitor structure to replace with something of equal strength: prefer polymorphic methods or a dispatch-table object when the tag set is stable, keep the tagged switch for tiny modules, and reach for JSDoc plus // @ts-check when an exhaustiveness checker (and therefore this pattern) is genuinely wanted.
pitfalls: The default arm is needed for a sane failure mode yet makes the switch non-exhaustive by construction: a new variant is a runtime error found by tests, never a build error.
Tags are strings: a typo ('cirlce') or a JSON payload with an unexpected tag is only caught at run time, because there is no type to seal.
A default that returns undefined or a neutral value instead of throwing turns a missed case into silent data corruption.
alternative: Dispatch on polymorphic methods (shape.area()) or a dispatch-table object keyed by the tag; when a real coverage guarantee is required, annotate the module with JSDoc union types and enable // @ts-check so TypeScript's never-based exhaustiveness check applies - JavaScript itself proves nothing at compile time.
